headline: DevOps Engineer Salary in the UK 2026: Averages by Level, City and Contract
metaDescription: DevOps engineer salary UK 2026: average near £53,400, junior £28-38k, senior £65-90k, London premium, contractor day rates and the skills that lift pay.

sections.content:
DevOps engineering remains one of the UK's best-paid technical disciplines in 2026. Glassdoor's 2026 data puts the national average at about £53,400 a year, while ONS-based benchmarks place typical permanent salaries between £55,000 and £85,000. Morgan McKinley's 2026 guide reports London averages of £65,000 to £80,000, and Robert Walters notes that London seniors with specialist cloud expertise stretch to £140,000.

The band data from ukcalculator tells the progression story: juniors (0-2 years) earn £32,000 to £45,000 nationally, mid-level engineers (2-5 years) £45,000 to £70,000, seniors £65,000 to £90,000, and leads or platform engineers £80,000 to £110,000. For true freshers with no prior IT job, realistic 2026 offers sit between £28,000 and £38,000, with a cloud certification or working automation on GitHub regularly pushing first offers past £38,000.
sections.title: 2026 Pay Benchmarks by Source

sections.content:
London is the UK's highest-paying city for DevOps at a median of about £81,250, roughly 25 percent above the national median. The South East follows at £71,500, with Scotland and the North West near £61,750, the Midlands at £60,450, and Wales at £59,800. London juniors earn £40,000 to £56,000 against £32,000 to £45,000 nationally, while London seniors reach £81,000 to £112,000 and leads £100,000 to £137,000.

Remote and hybrid working has narrowed but not closed the gap: regional employers can no longer assume a steep London discount, since engineers in Manchester or Leeds can often negotiate 20 to 35 percent more working remotely for a London firm. Set against that, London housing costs absorb much of the headline premium, so real-terms comparisons are closer than the raw figures suggest.
sections.title: London vs the Regions

sections.content:
Contracting pays a large premium over permanent roles. In 2026 UK DevOps contractors typically charge £300 to £450 a day at junior level, £450 to £650 mid-level, and £650 to £850 for seniors. Lead and platform engineers command £750 to £950, DevOps architects £850 to £1,200, and SREs £600 to £950. At 220 working days a year, £500 a day works out at about £110,000 before tax and expenses.

Since the 2021 off-payroll reforms, the client determines IR35 status for medium and large engagements, and outside-IR35 contracts pay noticeably more than inside ones. Recruiters actively filter on stated IR35 status, so contractors should confirm their Status Determination Statement before applying. Demand stays strong: the convergence of cloud-native infrastructure, platform engineering and SRE practice keeps DevOps among the most resilient hiring categories.
sections.title: Contractor Day Rates and IR35

sections.content:
Specialisation is the fastest lever on DevOps pay. Kubernetes expertise adds roughly £5,000 to £15,000 to salary, DevSecOps £5,000 to £10,000, and Terraform or infrastructure-as-code £4,000 to £8,000. An AWS Solutions Architect certification adds £5,000 to £9,000, Azure Expert £4,000 to £8,000, GitOps and ArgoCD £3,000 to £6,000, and observability tooling such as Datadog or Prometheus £3,000 to £6,000.

The pattern is clear: employers pay most for engineers who combine automation depth with security and cloud-platform breadth. Candidates who can show production Kubernetes, a working CI/CD pipeline and at least one major cloud certification negotiate from the strongest position at every seniority level.
